title: A short exact sequence of modules has a degreewise split short exact sequence of free resolutions
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $0\to Q\xrightarrow{u}Q'\xrightarrow{v}Q''\to0$ a short exact sequence of $R$-modules ($u$ injective, $\ker v=\operatorname{im}u$, $v$ surjective). Then there exist chain complexes of free $R$-modules $F_\bullet$, $F'_\bullet$, $F''_\bullet$ (indexed by $n\ge0$, differentials $d,d',d''$) with $R$-linear augmentations $\varepsilon:F_0\to Q$, $\varepsilon':F'_0\to Q'$, $\varepsilon'':F''_0\to Q''$ such that the three augmented complexes $\cdots\to F_1\xrightarrow{d_1}F_0\xrightarrow{\varepsilon}Q\to0$, $\cdots\to F'_1\to F'_0\xrightarrow{\varepsilon'}Q'\to0$, $\cdots\to F''_1\to F''_0\xrightarrow{\varepsilon''}Q''\to0$ are exact (free resolutions), together with morphisms of complexes $\alpha:F_\bullet\to F'_\bullet$, $\beta:F'_\bullet\to F''_\bullet$ ($d'_n\alpha_n=\alpha_{n-1}d_n$, $d''_n\beta_n=\beta_{n-1}d'_n$) satisfying $\varepsilon'\alpha_0=u\varepsilon$ and $\varepsilon''\beta_0=v\varepsilon'$, and, for every $n\ge0$, $R$-linear maps $\pi_n:F'_n\to F_n$ and $s_n:F''_n\to F'_n$ (not required to commute with the differentials) with $\beta_n\alpha_n=0$, $\pi_n\alpha_n=\mathrm{id}_{F_n}$, $\beta_ns_n=\mathrm{id}_{F''_n}$ and $\alpha_n\pi_n+s_n\beta_n=\mathrm{id}_{F'_n}$. In particular $0\to F_n\xrightarrow{\alpha_n}F'_n\xrightarrow{\beta_n}F''_n\to0$ is split exact for every $n$.

proof.text: One step (Stacks 065P, first half of the proof; the source's $M',M,M''$ are here $A,A',A''$). Claim: for every short exact sequence $0\to A\xrightarrow{a}A'\xrightarrow{b}A''\to0$ of $R$-modules there are free $R$-modules $P,P',P''$, $R$-linear surjections $\eta:P\to A$, $\eta':P'\to A'$, $\eta'':P''\to A''$ and $R$-linear maps $\alpha:P\to P'$, $\beta:P'\to P''$, $\pi:P'\to P$, $s:P''\to P'$ with $\beta\alpha=0$, $\pi\alpha=\mathrm{id}_P$, $\beta s=\mathrm{id}_{P''}$, $\alpha\pi+s\beta=\mathrm{id}_{P'}$, $\eta'\alpha=a\eta$, $\eta''\beta=b\eta'$, and such that $\alpha$ maps $K=\ker\eta$ into $K'=\ker\eta'$, $\beta$ maps $K'$ into $K''=\ker\eta''$, and the restrictions give a short exact sequence $0\to K\xrightarrow{\alpha|_K}K'\xrightarrow{\beta|_{K'}}K''\to0$. Construction: pick generating families $(x_i)_{i\in I}$ of $A$ and $(z_j)_{j\in J}$ of $A''$ (for instance all elements), and for each $j$ choose $y_j\in A'$ with $b(y_j)=z_j$ ($b$ is surjective). Put $P=\bigoplus_{i\in I}R$, $P''=\bigoplus_{j\in J}R$, $P'=P\oplus P''$; these are free [def-weil-pbc-free-module], with the standard bases $(e_i)$, $(f_j)$, and $P'$ has the basis $(e_i,0)_{i}\cup(0,f_j)_{j}$. Let $\eta(e_i)=x_i$, $\eta''(f_j)=z_j$, $\eta'(p,q)=a(\eta(p))+\lambda(q)$ where $\lambda:P''\to A'$ is the $R$-linear map with $\lambda(f_j)=y_j$ (a linear map out of $\bigoplus_JR$ is given by any choice of images of the $f_j$), so $b\lambda=\eta''$. $\eta,\eta''$ are surjective since their images contain generating families. Let $\alpha(p)=(p,0)$, $\beta(p,q)=q$, $\pi(p,q)=p$, $s(q)=(0,q)$. The identities $\beta\alpha=0$, $\pi\alpha=\mathrm{id}$, $\beta s=\mathrm{id}$, $\alpha\pi+s\beta=\mathrm{id}$ are checked on $(p,q)$: $(p,0)+(0,q)=(p,q)$. Also $\eta'\alpha(p)=a\eta(p)$ and $\eta''\beta(p,q)=\eta''(q)=b\lambda(q)=b(a\eta(p)+\lambda(q))=b\eta'(p,q)$ as $ba=0$. Now apply [lem-weil-pbc-snake-lemma-modules] with $\Lambda=R$ to the commutative diagram with top row $P\xrightarrow{\alpha}P'\xrightarrow{\beta}P''\to0$ (exact: $\beta$ is surjective and $\ker\beta=P\oplus0=\operatorname{im}\alpha$, see [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence]), bottom row $0\to A\xrightarrow{a}A'\xrightarrow{b}A''$ (exact by hypothesis) and vertical maps $\eta,\eta',\eta''$ (the squares commute by the two identities just shown). It gives that $\ker\eta\xrightarrow{\alpha|}\ker\eta'\xrightarrow{\beta|}\ker\eta''\xrightarrow{\partial}\operatorname{coker}\eta\to\operatorname{coker}\eta'\to\operatorname{coker}\eta''$ is exact, with $\alpha|_K$ injective because $\alpha$ is. Since $\eta$ and $\eta''$ are surjective, $\operatorname{coker}\eta=\operatorname{coker}\eta''=0$, so $\beta|_{K'}:K'\to K''$ is surjective and $\operatorname{coker}\eta'=0$, i.e. $\eta'$ is surjective. Thus $0\to K\to K'\to K''\to0$ is short exact, which proves the claim (the source: 'By the snake lemma we see that the sequence of kernels $0\to K'\to K\to K''\to0$ is short exact').

proof.text: Iteration (Stacks 065P: 'Hence we can continue this process indefinitely'). Define by recursion on $n\ge0$ a short exact sequence $E_n:0\to A_n\xrightarrow{a_n}A'_n\xrightarrow{b_n}A''_n\to0$ and the data of Step 1 for it. Start with $E_0=(0\to Q\xrightarrow{u}Q'\xrightarrow{v}Q''\to0)$. Given $E_n$, apply Step 1 to $E_n$ and call the result $F_n=P$, $F'_n=P'$, $F''_n=P''$, $\eta_n:F_n\to A_n$, $\eta'_n$, $\eta''_n$, $\alpha_n$, $\beta_n$, $\pi_n$, $s_n$; then let $E_{n+1}$ be the short exact sequence of kernels $0\to\ker\eta_n\xrightarrow{\alpha_n|}\ker\eta'_n\xrightarrow{\beta_n|}\ker\eta''_n\to0$ given by Step 1, so $A_{n+1}=\ker\eta_n\subseteq F_n$, $A'_{n+1}=\ker\eta'_n\subseteq F'_n$, $A''_{n+1}=\ker\eta''_n\subseteq F''_n$, and $a_{n+1},b_{n+1}$ are the restrictions of $\alpha_n,\beta_n$. Write $j_n:A_{n+1}\to F_n$, $j'_n$, $j''_n$ for the inclusions, so that $\alpha_nj_n=j'_na_{n+1}$ and $\beta_nj'_n=j''_nb_{n+1}$. Put $\varepsilon=\eta_0$, $\varepsilon'=\eta'_0$, $\varepsilon''=\eta''_0$ and, for $n\ge0$, $d_{n+1}=j_n\eta_{n+1}:F_{n+1}\to F_n$, $d'_{n+1}=j'_n\eta'_{n+1}$, $d''_{n+1}=j''_n\eta''_{n+1}$. (Each stage involves choices; a recursive definition with a choice at each stage is the usual one, by dependent choice.)

proof.text: Verification. Each $F_n,F'_n,F''_n$ is free by Step 1 [def-weil-pbc-free-module]. Complexes and exactness [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence], written for the unprimed sequence (the primed and double-primed ones are identical): $\varepsilon d_1=\eta_0j_0\eta_1=0$ and $d_nd_{n+1}=j_{n-1}\eta_nj_n\eta_{n+1}=0$ for $n\ge1$, since $\eta_nj_n=0$ ($j_n$ is the inclusion of $\ker\eta_n$). $\varepsilon=\eta_0$ is surjective. Since $\eta_{n+1}$ is surjective onto $A_{n+1}=\ker\eta_n$, $\operatorname{im}d_{n+1}=j_n(A_{n+1})=\ker\eta_n$; and $\ker\eta_0=\ker\varepsilon$, while for $n\ge1$ $\ker d_n=\ker(j_{n-1}\eta_n)=\ker\eta_n$ because $j_{n-1}$ is injective. So $\operatorname{im}d_1=\ker\varepsilon$ and $\operatorname{im}d_{n+1}=\ker d_n$: the augmented complex $\cdots\to F_1\to F_0\xrightarrow{\varepsilon}Q\to0$ is exact. Morphisms of complexes: by Step 1 for $E_{n+1}$, $\eta'_{n+1}\alpha_{n+1}=a_{n+1}\eta_{n+1}$, hence $d'_{n+1}\alpha_{n+1}=j'_n\eta'_{n+1}\alpha_{n+1}=j'_na_{n+1}\eta_{n+1}=\alpha_nj_n\eta_{n+1}=\alpha_nd_{n+1}$; likewise $d''_{n+1}\beta_{n+1}=j''_nb_{n+1}\eta'_{n+1}=\beta_nj'_n\eta'_{n+1}=\beta_nd'_{n+1}$. The augmentation identities are those of Step 1 for $E_0$: $\varepsilon'\alpha_0=u\varepsilon$, $\varepsilon''\beta_0=v\varepsilon'$. Finally $\beta_n\alpha_n=0$, $\pi_n\alpha_n=\mathrm{id}$, $\beta_ns_n=\mathrm{id}$, $\alpha_n\pi_n+s_n\beta_n=\mathrm{id}$ hold by Step 1 for $E_n$; they give that $\alpha_n$ is injective, $\beta_n$ surjective and $\ker\beta_n=\operatorname{im}\alpha_n$ (if $\beta_n(x)=0$ then $x=\alpha_n\pi_n(x)$), i.e. $0\to F_n\to F'_n\to F''_n\to0$ is split exact, which is the source's 'each of the sequences $0\to F'_n\to F_n\to F''_n\to0$ is split exact (by construction)'.
